item: A redirect hop to another host reads its robots.txt and waits its interval first, a crawl kept to one site refuses a hop off it, and a redirect to an address written with a login is never followed (R629, R633)
summary: R629 (Plan's ruling on R624's independent read: "an on-site link that 302-redirects to another host is followed with no scope check and no robots.txt read for that host") and R633 (ruled on a review's measurement, folded in as its own commit). BEFORE: src/ingest/__init__.py _guarded_redirect_get re-ran the parser check and the SSRF guard on a hop and nothing else, so a page whose host answered 302 to another host was followed there with no robots.txt read and no wait for that host's interval or Crawl-delay, inside the first host's lock: a disallowing or unreadable robots.txt refused another host's pages when they were asked for and let them through when a redirect led there, and another thread could reach that host at the same moment. A crawl kept to one site (CrawlConfig.same_domain_only) followed an on-site link that redirected off the site and stored the other site's page as its own, and a sitemap on the host that redirected off it was fetched and its URLs taken. A Location that wrote a user name or password was followed: measured on 2c26ff4ac, a plain on-site link that 302s to https://alice:hunter2@good.example/landing was requested with Authorization: Basic YWxpY2U6aHVudGVyMg== and came back as the page's final and canonical URL (ingest_url stored it). NOW (R629): a page fetch carries a _RedirectChain (src/ingest/__init__.py:1026), and a hop to another host key (_host_netloc: the host and the port; the scheme alone is not another host, so an http to https upgrade on one host is unchanged) is a first request to that host (_take_hop_host, :1985): the switch is read; the chain's lock moves to the new host; its robots.txt is read (_enforce_robots, fail-closed: RobotsDisallowed or RobotsUnavailable with its cause, the same types a first request gets, the sentence ending in the fixed words "(reached by a redirect)", cached and backed off as a first read is); its interval or Crawl-delay is waited, or past the cap deferred (CrawlDelayDeferred, the next-allowed-at written first); the switch is read again (a Stop pressed during the lock wait or the interval refuses the hop). THE LOCK IS HANDED OVER, NEVER STACKED: the host left is stamped (its request was answered) and its lock released before the next lock is waited for, so a thread holds at most one host lock and two chains crossing each other (A to B on one thread, B to A on another) cannot deadlock; the hop's request and body read are under the new host's lock, so no other thread reaches that host meanwhile. A retry starts again from the first host (chain.move(chain.first)); a hop that defers on a retry reports the failed request before it, the rule the first host already had. A hop past the bound reads nothing (_MAX_REDIRECTS stays 5). The robots read (_get_robots, so declared_sitemaps too) and the two preflights pass no chain: their own hops keep today's behaviour and never read robots.txt, so a read cannot recurse. fetch(redirect_scope=) refuses a hop the scope does not cover, or cannot judge (it raises), with RedirectOutOfScope (a FetchFailed, :187) before the hop's host is looked up; crawl.py hands the site under same_domain_only (_kept_on_site, the _off_site test a harvested link takes, so a hop whose authority holds an @ is off the site too) and sitemap.py hands its host (the rule its off-host children already follow; the refused sitemap is written in errors). Both are counted as fetch_failed (classified "other"); www.good.example is the same site and another host, so its robots.txt is read before it. NOW (R633): a hop whose Location writes a userinfo (_carries_userinfo on the Location, :1945) is refused as a BlockedTarget (the type of R622's refusals of the address beside it, so a fetcher held to one host, scripts/law_pit_real_run.py, still reads it as a refused hop) in fixed words, "redirect to an address that carries a user name or password, not followed: " and the address through failure_url, after R622's parser check and before the scope, the guard and anything asked of the host, for every caller, robots reads included (a robots read that meets one is fail-closed, cause unreachable). The Location is read, not the joined URL: a relative Location writes no authority and keeps the one of the request it answers, so an address the caller wrote with a login keeps it on that host as before, and any Location that writes one is refused, the caller's own login included. TESTS: tests/test_redirect_hop_robots_r629.py, 55, through the real EthicalFetcher, crawl_source, discover_sitemap_urls, ingest_url and the preflight's _check_one over an in-memory session (every planted URL routed, so a follow is seen), a fake clock (a wait is recorded, never slept), every fetch in a bounded thread; the switch control and the R633 tests on a real requests.Session over an in-memory adapter that records every request's URL and headers. 40 fail on 2c26ff4ac (32 R629, 8 R633), the 15 controls pass (a robots read's own hop and declared_sitemaps read no robots.txt on the other host; a same-host hop, an http to https upgrade and a same-host hop to a disallowed path are unchanged; the hop past the bound; the crossing chains; an on-site hop and a www. sitemap followed; a Stop as the first host answers on a real session; the preflight ping; an @ in a path, query or fragment followed; an operator's login kept on a relative hop). On f7d064626 (R629 alone) only the 8 R633 tests fail. The three _http_get test stubs (tests/test_crawl_delay_retry_is_a_failure.py, tests/test_robots_read_refused_by_switch.py) take **_kw for the new chain keyword. RELATED: related run on cf02ee603 (232 related test files and the new file): 8,044 passed, 12 skipped, 4 failed, each failing the same way on 2c26ff4ac (tests/test_csv_feeds.py::test_feeds_api_list_and_import; tests/test_workflow_integration.py::test_full_investigative_workflow; tests/test_shared_file_writes.py::test_no_new_unlocked_write_site_and_no_stale_allowance, the same three unlocked write sites in src/ingest/__init__.py, 417, 549 and 713 on the base; tests/test_xdist_file_placement.py::test_a_real_run_announces_the_fixed_placement, pytest-xdist not installed here). A first run with R633's refusal a plain FetchFailed failed tests/test_law_pit_real_run.py's two userinfo-hop cases, which expect BlockedTarget; the refusal is a BlockedTarget now and that test is unchanged. ruff F,B clean; ruff ratchet 412; mypy clean on the three source files. Mutants, in a detached worktree, all killed: R629 18 (no robots read on the hop; no interval; the next lock taken on top of the first, killed by the crossing-chains test alone, which reports the deadlock; every caller's hop reading robots, so robots reads recurse; the crawl or the sitemap handing no scope; the scope asked after the guard and the robots read; same-host hops treated as another host; a hop deferral on a retry reported as a deferral; the host left not stamped; no switch read before or after the hop's waits; a scope that raises letting the hop through; the lock released on success only; the unrequested last hop reading robots; the "(reached by a redirect)" words dropped; the hop's host not stamped after its request; a retry not going back to the first host). R633 9 (no check; the request answered read instead of the Location; robots reads unchecked; the joined URL read, refusing an inherited login; only a changed authority refused; the address written raw; the check after the hop has taken its host; the check before R622's parser check, killed by two R622 tests whose refusal words it changes; the refusal as a plain FetchFailed). NOT CHANGED, stated: a same-host hop takes no can_fetch for its new path (the first request's decision stands; pinned as unchanged); an http to https upgrade never reads the https robots.txt; the preflight's homepage ping (src/monitoring/preflight.py:138) is made whatever robots.txt says and its hops keep today's behaviour (R633 still applies to them); a feed or sitemap page address (ingest_url) that redirects to another site is still followed, now after that host's robots.txt and interval, and stored as the source's article (only the crawl and the sitemap index are kept to one site); a hop's request rides the first host's Tor circuit as before while its robots.txt read rides the hop host's own (as any read of that host does); a transient failure at a hop is still worded against the URL asked for; a sitemap urlset's page addresses are not host-checked (ruled R626 and R627). FOLD (Steward 3's security read and the independent read, both GO with should-fixes; new commits, none amended): a hop's deferral, the hop host's Crawl-delay, said neither that host nor the redirect, so ingest_url and law/track.py filed it against the page asked for; its sentence ("Crawl-delay <n> s: not before <time>", which nothing parses: the readers key on the type and on the "deferred: " prefix law/track.py writes, read by src/api/law.py _verdict_of) is now followed by ", for '<the hop's address through failure_url>' (reached by a redirect)" (_respect_rate_limit's hop_url, :2406). robots.txt compared an EMPTY path with what follows it (RobotFileParser read https://b.example?x as "?x", which "Disallow: /" does not cover, while requests asks for /?x; it predates R629 and direct fetches had it): _enforce_robots checks such an address as the same address with the path "/" (:2230), for EVERY fetch, a direct one as well as a hop, so this one is a behaviour change beyond the redirect work. A retry's back-off slept inside the hop host's lock ([(0.5, ['b.example'])]): the chain moves back to the first host before the sleep (:1572), the one move a retry makes (the loop-top move, then redundant, removed). Tests pin where the reads' mutants survived: A -> B -> A waits A's interval again under A's lock and stamps A again; the hop's robots read and wait run under B's lock with A's released; each refusal (scope, a Location with a login, robots disallowed, robots unavailable, a deferral) leaves both locks free and never stamps B; a KeyboardInterrupt at the hop's robots read, wait or request leaves no lock held; a cached disallowing robots.txt refuses the hop; the host left is stamped before its lock is released; robots.txt before the interval; the hop's robots read on the circuit of its host key. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated: a crawl kept to its site whose start URL redirects to another subdomain (cnn.com to edition.cnn.com; _off_site strips only www.) is refused at the hop and counted as fetch_failed, where before R629 it stored that one page and harvested nothing from it; pinned. The file holds 81 tests: on 17576d851 7 fail (the deferral's words, 5 empty-path cases, the back-off) and 74 pass. Fold mutants 14, all killed (the reads' M27, M17, M26, M18, M4, M9 and M13 re-made among them); the earlier matrices on the fold head: R629 17 and R633 9 killed (the eighteenth R629 mutant, a retry not going back to the first host, became equivalent and is the fold's N4). Related run on 8c73caa5d (the 232 related test files and the new file): 8,069 passed, 12 skipped, 5 failed, each failing the same way on 2c26ff4ac: the four of the earlier run, and tests/test_file_lock.py::test_an_interrupt_in_the_hold_statistic_after_the_section_leaves_nothing_held, a timing race in a test and a module this branch does not touch (BlockingIOError in 13 of 88 runs under load on 2c26ff4ac; 5 of 5 pass alone on the fold head). The reads' numbers: 84,000 scope-fuzz fetches with 0 off-site requests under a scope; 8 threads with at most 1 request in flight per host and 0 interval breaks (the base: up to 3 in flight, 101 of 150 broken); 16,050 Locations with 0 Authorization headers sent. At the merge of R621 and R622 (Steward 3's note): _take_hop_host now runs inside R622's outer except ValueError round the redirect loop, so a ValueError raised while a hop moves the chain, reads the other host's robots.txt or waits its interval (no known input raises one there: _host_netloc never raises and the robots read has its own handler) reads as R622's FetchFailed "redirect to a URL that cannot be read, from " and the URL that answered the redirect, with no context, the hop's page never requested and no lock left held; pinned by 3 tests, so the file now holds 84. Stated, not fixed: a Location with no // such as http:alice:hunter2@b.example/x is refused as unsupported and its text written raw (urlparse sees no userinfo; it predates R633); a Unicode host and its punycode spelling are two host keys, so two locks (R621's area); the guard looks up a hop at the redirect bound that is never requested. The same-host path hop, the http to https upgrade and the preflight ping are ruled R636, built by another session on top of this branch. Release-notes lines: «A page that redirects to another site is now followed only after that site's robots.txt allows it and its politeness wait has passed, and a crawl kept to one site no longer follows a redirect off it. (R629)» Proposed for the empty path (Plan's line not set yet): «A web address with no path before its query, such as https://example.org?page=2, is now checked against its site's robots.txt as the page it actually fetches, so a site that disallows everything is no longer fetched through such an address. (R629)» Proposed for R633 (Plan's line not set yet): «A page that redirects to an address written with a user name or password is no longer followed. (R633)»
